description: Makes cost feel knowable and affordable. It covers flat-rate prices or 'starting at' figures, good/better/best tiers, maintenance-plan memberships, monthly financing payments and estimate builders. It's often the section that turns a nervous homeowner into a quote request.
queries: membership plans pricing section for a consumer service
service price list section with starting prices

references.layout: A full-bleed colored section with a left-aligned 1-line heading ending in an asterisk. Two equal cards side by side (~14px radius) hold the brand option and the alternative. Each has a label top-left, a huge monthly figure with a small term note beside it, then a label column and an em-dash bullet column. A 2-line footnote spans the bottom.
references.type: Heading in a light neo-grotesk at ~32px. Monthly figures in the same light grotesk at ~56px ('$1,896/mo'), with '/mo' at the same size and the term ('for 30 years') at ~9px. Bullets ~10px with em-dash markers. Footnote ~8px.
references.color: Bright azure ~#0A8CF0 ground, white type. The brand card is solid black ~#000000; the competitor card is a deeper blue ~#0B6FC0.
details: The comparison is the whole section: our monthly payment against the typical alternative
Em-dash bullets ('— 6.5% APR — 30½ year term — $0/mo for 6 months') read like a fact sheet
The black brand card on blue makes the recommended option pop with no badge
The asterisked footnote holds the assumptions, which builds trust
references.why_it_works: It turns a scary total into a monthly number and proves it's better than the obvious alternative. Huge light-weight numerals feel calm, not salesy.
references.trade_adaptation: HVAC or roofing: 'What you could pay:*' with '$189/mo — our financing (9.99% APR, 60 months, $0 down)' vs '$312/mo — typical credit card (24% APR)', and the assumptions ('$9,000 system…') in the footnote.

references.layout: A left-aligned heading. Below, a table with row labels in the left ~20% and five option columns. The brand's column is a solid black rounded (~8px) pillar that extends above the header row and below the last row. The other columns are separated only by thin vertical dividers. A centered pill button sits under the table.
references.type: Heading in a light neo-grotesk at ~34px. Column headers ~10px regular, centered, 2 lines. Row labels ~10px. The marks are thin checks and light grey '×'.
references.color: White ground, black ~#000000 pillar with white checks, grey ~#BDBDBD crosses, dividers ~#E8E8E8. Azure ~#0A8CF0 pill CTA.
details: The recommended option is a solid inverted column, not a 'Most popular' badge
Competitor columns use pale grey crosses, so they recede
No horizontal row lines; spacing alone separates the rows
The CTA names the next step: 'Get your rate estimate'
references.why_it_works: One glance shows that the brand ticks every box. The inverted pillar is a strong but elegant way to show a recommendation.
references.trade_adaptation: Financing page: 'Our in-house financing' vs 'Credit card' vs 'HELOC' vs 'Personal loan', with rows such as 'No payments for 6 months', 'No home appraisal', 'Approval in minutes', 'Covers install & permits'.

references.layout: A large left-aligned statement (~5 lines, max ~440px) that names the pain. Below is a 3x2 grid of hand-drawn illustrations (~110px tall), each with a 3-line caption under it, left-aligned to the illustration. A centered pill button closes the section.
references.type: Statement in a neo-grotesk at ~24px light, line-height ~1.2. Captions ~10px regular.
references.color: Off-white ~#F6F5EF ground, ink ~#1A1A1A line drawings with lime ~#9AD34A and yellow accents, azure ~#0A8CF0 button.
details: The opening statement admits the pain ('It can be painful to finance…') before offering the fix
Loose, human hand-drawn illustrations (a person watering a plant, a calendar, a truck) instead of icon fonts
Captions are concrete terms ('No payments and no interest for the first six months…')
references.why_it_works: It makes financing feel humane and simple, and the illustrations add warmth to a dry topic without looking like stock.
references.trade_adaptation: Remodeler or HVAC financing block: 'A new furnace shouldn't wreck your budget.' Benefits: 'No payments for 6 months', 'Finance 100% incl. install', 'Soft credit check', 'Pay off early, no penalty', each with a simple ink drawing in the brand accent.

references.layout: Centered: heading, a 2-line sub, a 'Your purchase' label and a big amount. A slider (~400px) has a circular handle with a '<>' glyph. Below are full-width stacked pill rows (~30px radius, ~60px tall, ~10px gaps). Each row has a bold plan name with a small detail line on the left, and a bold amount with a small 'Total cost' line on the right.
references.type: Heading in a condensed heavy grotesk at ~26px. Amount ~28px bold. Row titles ~13px bold, detail lines ~9px regular. Right-hand amounts ~13px bold, right-aligned.
references.color: White ground, near-black ~#17120F type, pill rows in warm off-white ~#F5F3EE, slider track ~#E0E0E0 with a black filled segment.
details: Each option shows total cost and total interest, which is transparent rather than a teaser
The slider sets one input and every row updates, keeping the interaction minimal
The '<>' glyph on the handle says 'drag me' without instructions
references.why_it_works: Visitors can play with their own project size and see real monthly figures. It's interactive, honest and simple.
references.trade_adaptation: 'Estimate your monthly payment': a 'Your project' slider ($2k-$40k), then rows for '12 months, 0% APR', '36 months, 7.99%' and '60 months, 9.99%', each with monthly and total cost, plus a 'Pre-qualify — no credit impact' button.

references.layout: Left ~35%: an all-caps eyebrow, a heading, a 3-line sub and an underlined link with an arrow. Center: a floating white UI card (~190px wide, ~10px radius, soft shadow) titled 'Choose your plan' with three radio rows. The selected row expands to show APR, Interest and Total and has a purple 'Interest free' tag. A full-width Continue button sits at the bottom. Cut-out 3D product renders (sofas) sit around the card at angles, with a half-circle sticker.
references.type: Heading in a neo-grotesk at ~32px medium. Eyebrow ~9px bold all caps. Card text ~10-12px, with bold amounts ('$300.00 / month').
references.color: Pale grey-green ~#EEF0EA ground, ink ~#111111, Shop purple ~#5A31F4 for the selected state, button and tag, red-orange ~#FF5B2E sticker.
details: A real-looking plan selector UI used as the illustration
The selected row shows the breakdown (APR 0%, Interest $0, Total $1800)
Cut-out product photos break out of the grid around the card
A rotated sticker 'DREAM BIG PAY SMALL' adds personality
references.why_it_works: It demonstrates the payment options instead of describing them, and the cut-outs make it feel like a retail ad rather than a fintech page.
references.trade_adaptation: Water heater or garage-door install: a floating 'Choose your plan' card ('$95/mo · 12 months · 0% APR' selected) surrounded by cut-out photos of a tankless heater, a new door and a smiling tech, plus a brand-color sticker 'NO MONEY DOWN'.

references.layout: Full-bleed color section with a centered 2-line heading. Three white cards (~10px radius). Each has a black-and-white engraved-style illustration at the top that grows by tier (sprout → leafy branch → full tree), a hairline, a title, a bold subtitle, 'What's included' with shield-check items, and a full-width black button pinned to the bottom.
references.type: Heading in a geometric grotesk at ~30px medium, white. Tier titles ~18px regular. Subtitles ~10px bold. Items ~9-10px.
references.color: Bright orange ~#FF5A1F ground with a faint dot pattern, white cards, black ~#111111 buttons and text, grey ~#555555 icons. The illustrations are monochrome halftone/engraving.
details: The illustration grows from sprout to tree, explaining good/better/best with no words
Engraving-style art feels like old print, distinctive and timeless
Every card's CTA is the same 'Get a quote', so no tier is pushed
Shield-check icons match the 'protection' theme
references.why_it_works: Tiers become intuitive through an image metaphor, and the orange-plus-engraving combination is unusual and memorable.
references.trade_adaptation: Roofing or maintenance tiers: 'Repair' (a single shingle), 'Restore' (a section of roof), 'Replace' (a whole house), drawn as engravings that build up, each with 'Get a quote'. For a landscaper the sprout-to-tree metaphor fits literally.

references.layout: A centered 2-line heading (the second line lighter) over angled background stripes. Two side-by-side cards with the right one offset ~30px lower. The left white card has a colored label, a description, a huge price, a caption, three icon bullets and a footer strip link. The right dark card has a label, a description, a 2x2 hairline grid of custom options and a footer link.
references.type: Heading in a light grotesk at ~24px. Price ~40px light ('2.9%') with a small superscript-like '+ 30¢'. Labels ~10px all caps with tracking. Body ~11px.
references.color: Mint-to-lime ~#9EDC9B/#D8F2B5 angled stripes, white card with green ~#3ECF8E label, dark navy ~#32325D card with lavender ~#CFD7FF text, footer strip ~#F6F9FC.
details: Contrast between a simple standard price and 'Let's design a custom package'
The vertical offset between the cards makes the pair feel composed
Footer strips act as full-width buttons ('GET STARTED IN MINUTES →', 'CONTACT SALES →')
A 2x2 hairline grid lists what can be customized
references.why_it_works: It maps exactly to how trades price: standard jobs at a flat rate, bigger jobs by custom quote. It shows both honestly side by side.
references.trade_adaptation: Plumber: 'FLAT-RATE: Drain clearing $149 · No overtime fees · Price before we start' vs 'CUSTOM QUOTE: Repiping · Sewer line · Remodels · Commercial', with 'BOOK NOW →' and 'GET A FREE ESTIMATE →'.

references.layout: A left column holds a 2-line, two-color heading and a 1-line sub. Three tier columns each have a small line icon, the tier name, a 3-line description, the price and an outlined or filled pill CTA. The top tier's column is tinted from header to table bottom and has a hand-drawn hat illustration perched on its top edge. Feature rows are grouped by hairlines, with centered values and checks.
references.type: Heading in a rounded grotesk at ~24px. Tier names ~20px. Prices ~16px bold ('$49 /year', with '/year' smaller). CTAs ~9px bold all caps with an arrow. Row labels ~9px bold.
references.color: Butter cream ~#FFFDF2 ground, deep teal ~#1F3B3A text, burgundy ~#6B1E2E second heading line, peach ~#F6D5C0 top-tier column, violet-blue ~#4A3AFF filled CTA.
details: An illustrated hat sits on top of the premium column, a playful 'crown'
Small line icons above each tier name (globe, sparkle, gem) differentiate the tiers
The two-color heading ('Compare' in teal, 'memberships' in burgundy) is a warm, editorial touch
The free tier uses words ('Always free') instead of $0
references.why_it_works: A friendly, warm take on the comparison table. The tinted column plus a small illustration marks the recommendation with character instead of a badge.
references.trade_adaptation: HVAC or plumbing maintenance club: 'Basic' (1 tune-up/yr), 'Comfort' (2 tune-ups + 10% off), 'Priority' (tinted, with a little illustrated wrench or hard hat on top: same-day service, no overtime fees, 15% off).

references.layout: A centered serif heading, a 2-line sub and a 'Pay monthly / Pay yearly' toggle with a tiny 'Save 30%!' note. Three equal cards (~6px radius), each tinted differently, each with an optional small tag pill, the price, a 3-line description, a check list and a black full-width button. Paid tiers carry a diagonal corner ribbon reading 'save 30%' in the tier color.
references.type: Heading in a book serif at ~30px regular. Prices in the serif at ~24px ('$52 / year' with '($1 per week)' at ~8px). Tag pills ~7px bold all caps. Body ~10px grotesk.
references.color: White ground. Cards tinted grey ~#F1F2F0, sage ~#E9EFE6 and lilac ~#F3ECF1. Tags in sage ~#7C9A72 and mauve ~#B48AA6. Black ~#111111 buttons.
details: The per-week breakdown under the annual price ('$1 per week') makes the cost tiny
Each tier has its own tint, with the tag and ribbon in a darker shade of the same tint
A heart icon replaces the check on the last item of the top tier: a human touch
The serif price feels bookish and warm rather than SaaS
references.why_it_works: Soft tints and a serif make tiers feel personal and approachable, and the per-week reframe is a simple affordability trick.
references.trade_adaptation: Lawn or pool care plans: 'Essential', 'Seasonal' (sage), 'Full-Service' (clay), with '$39/visit ($9 a week)' and a corner ribbon 'Save 15% prepaid'.

references.layout: Two columns. The left ~62% holds category blocks, each with an icon + title header, line items with right-aligned editable amount boxes (~50px), and a tinted 'Total' row. Each block is followed by a row of 'fits your budget' chips ('Under $40'). The right ~25% is a sticky 'Cost Breakdown' panel listing the category subtotals, with a bold grand total.
references.type: Category headers in a grotesk at ~20px medium. Line items ~10px. Amounts ~9px inside input boxes. Totals bold.
references.color: White ground, near-black text, total rows and side panel in pale mint ~#EEF5EE, chip borders ~#D5D5D5, green ~#14A800 brand accent.
details: Editable amount boxes invite the visitor to build their own budget
The sticky side panel keeps the running total visible while scrolling
Budget chips under each block suggest options at that price
references.why_it_works: It makes a complex, multi-part job transparent. Visitors see how the price is built and can adjust it, which builds trust before the quote.
references.trade_adaptation: Bathroom remodel estimator: categories 'Demolition', 'Plumbing', 'Tile & finishes', 'Fixtures', each with typical line-item ranges, and a sticky 'Your estimate: $14,200–$18,900' panel with a 'Get an exact quote' button.

references.layout: Top-left: the heading set on two cream label blocks, like stickers. Top-right: a short paragraph. Below, a 'What's Included' card with a check list on the left (~45%). On the right, stacked tier cards, each with title, price, a dashed rule, a qualifier line, another dashed rule and a full-width black button. The second tier card is outlined in yellow.
references.type: Heading in a book serif at ~24px with key words in red. Tier titles and prices in the serif at ~20px. Qualifiers ~11px serif. Check items ~8px grotesk.
references.color: Deep green ~#1E5A1E ground, cream ~#F7F0DC label blocks, red ~#D8332A emphasis words, white cards with a 2px black border and a hard ~4px black offset shadow, a yellow ~#F2C94C outline on the highlighted tier.
details: Hard offset shadows and thick borders give a retro, print or sign-painter feel
The heading sits on cream 'label-maker' strips
Dashed rules separate price from qualifier, like a receipt
Features are listed once in a shared card, so tiers differ only by scope
references.why_it_works: A rare pricing layout with real character: old-school, sturdy and honest. Listing the shared features once keeps the tier cards short.
references.trade_adaptation: Old-school family plumbing or HVAC: green ground, 'Every visit includes:' card (licensed tech, upfront price, shoe covers, clean-up), then tier cards 'Service call $89', 'Tune-up $149', 'Comfort Club $19/mo' with the club outlined in the accent color.

references.layout: A centered grey eyebrow that frames value ('What could cost you $15,000 is $499'), then a centered heading. On the left, a credit-card-shaped object (~270x165, ~14px radius) with a soft glow shadow shows the brand and the price, with a 2-line reassurance and a full-width orange pill CTA below it. On the right, three check items, each with a bold title and a 3-line description.
references.type: Heading in a neo-grotesk at ~26px regular. Card price ~22px bold white ('$42/month'). Item titles ~12px medium, body ~9px grey. Eyebrow ~12px grey.
references.color: White ground, a card in organic orange texture ~#FF5A1F/#FF8A3D with an orange glow shadow, an orange ~#FF5A1F pill button, check icons in orange.
details: The plan is shown as a physical membership card, something people can picture owning
The value anchor sits in the eyebrow ('could cost you $15,000')
A refund reassurance line sits right under the card
references.why_it_works: For a single plan, the card makes the membership feel tangible and premium, and the anchor makes the price feel small.
references.trade_adaptation: HVAC 'Comfort Club' or pest-control annual plan: a brand-colored member card '$19/month, billed annually at $228', with an eyebrow 'One emergency call can cost $450' and checks for '2 tune-ups a year', 'No overtime fees', 'Priority scheduling'.

takeaways: Lead with the monthly number, set big and light, with APR, term and assumptions in small print or an asterisked footnote. Trades sell big-ticket jobs, and monthly framing plus visible disclosure builds trust.
Compare against the obvious alternative (credit card, HELOC, 'typical' price) rather than only against your own tiers.
Mark the recommended option with an inverted solid column, a tinted column or a growing illustration, not a generic 'Most popular' badge.
Calculators and sliders that show monthly and total cost make financing tangible and honest. One input, many updated rows.
Match how trades actually price: flat-rate standard jobs next to custom-quote projects, or a shared 'every visit includes' list with tiers that differ only by scope.
Warmth comes from serif prices, tinted cards, hand-drawn or engraved illustration and earthy grounds, not SaaS blue and gradients.
Reframe cost small ('$1 per week', 'could cost you $15,000') and show reassurances (refund, no money down, soft credit check) next to the CTA.
Every pricing block ends in a concrete next step ('Get your rate estimate', 'Get a quote'), not 'Learn more'.
avoid: The standard SaaS 3-column grid with a purple 'Most popular' pill, a Monthly/Yearly toggle and an 'Enterprise: Let's talk' column (Riverside, Height, Customer.io): wrong vocabulary for a local trade.
Dark neon pricing cards with glowing gradient buttons (Save.design, ClickUp add-ons): reads as a crypto or AI tool.
Glowing purple-gradient hero backgrounds behind the plans (Mixpanel).
Giant feature-comparison matrices with 20+ rows of checkmarks (Threads, Webflow site plans). Homeowners need 4-6 rows at most.
Per-seat or per-unit pricing language and footnote soup copied from software.
Icon-in-square 'add-on' cards with blue 'Learn more' buttons (Webflow add-ons): generic and non-committal.
Prices hidden behind 'Contact us' with no starting point at all. Show 'from $X' even when jobs are quoted.
